newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronic stocks up on foreign fund hopes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronic stocks up on foreign fund hopes.

text.p: Taiwan's electronic shares rose at mid-morning on Tuesday on hopes of a new influx of foreign funds following the government's decision to raise its ceiling on foreign ownership of domestic stocks, brokers said.
The ceiling will rise to 25 percent from 20 percent in any one listed firm by the end of 1996.
After succumbing to profit-taking on Monday, electronics saw strong interest as soon as the market opened on Tuesday.
"Fundamentals in the industry are good and hopes for foreign funds in the sector further helped buying," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment Services.

After 70 minutes, most-active issue Mosel, a semiconductor manufacturer, was up 40 cents or 1.15 percent to T$35.20. It was followed by electronic appliance maker Tatung, which gained T$1.6 or 3.27 percent to T$50.50.
Computer giant Acer was the third-most active issue, rising 80 cents or two percent to T$40.90.
